newsitem.title: USA: Ross carrying Clinton messages to Arafat, Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Ross carrying Clinton messages to Arafat, Netanyahu.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross is carrying messages from President Bill Clinton to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on his mission to tackle the latest crisis in the Middle East peace process, the State Department said on Wednesday.
Spokesman John Dinger also told reporters that Ross intended to return to Washington this weekend to report to Clinton after meeting Arafat in Rabat and Netanyahu in Israel.

U.S. officials said the decision to send Ross to the Middle East was made after Secretary of State Madeleine Albright spoke to Arafat by telephone Tuesday night while she was travelling back to Washington from a day spent in North Carolina with Republican Sen. Jesse Helms, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Commitese Helms.

Tensions have risen in the region after a decision by Netanyahu to proceed with a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv by militant Palestinians. Netanyahu has accused Arafat of giving militants a "green light" to launch attacks on the Jewish state.
"President Clinton wants Dennis Ross to provide him with an assessment of the situation," Dinger said. "He is taking presidential messages with him."
The United States is again trying to get Netanyahu and Arafat back into direct talks in hopes of calming the situation and getting peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians back on track.
